1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Paul, an apostle (sent one), not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised Jesus from the dead,
And all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,
Who gave Himself for our sins, that He might deliver (rescue) us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father,
To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I marvel (am amazed) that you are so soon removed (turned away) from Him who called you into the grace of Christ, to another gospel (good news),
Which is not another. But there are some who trouble you, and would pervert (twist) the gospel (good news) of Christ.
But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel (good news) to you than that which we have preached to you, let that one be accursed (cursed by God).
As we said before, so I say now again: If anyone preaches any other gospel (good news) to you than that which you have received, let that person be accursed (cursed by God).
For do I now persuade (try to win over) people, or God? Or do I seek to please people? For if I yet pleased people, I would not be the servant of Christ.
But I certify (make known to) you, brothers, that the gospel (good news) which was preached by me is not after man (from people).
For I neither received it from man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation (showing) of Jesus Christ.
For you have heard of my conversation (way of life) in time past in the Jews' religion, how beyond measure I persecuted (attacked for faith) the church of God, and wasted (destroyed) it,
And profited (went ahead) in the Jews' religion above many my equals (of my own age) in my own nation, being more exceedingly zealous (eager) for the traditions of my fathers.
But when it pleased God, who separated (set) me apart from my mother's womb, and called me by His grace,
To reveal (show) His Son in me, that I might preach Him among the heathen (people who are not Jews), immediately I did not confer (talk it over) with flesh and blood (any human).
Neither did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles (sent ones) before me. But I went into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.
Then after 3 years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode (stayed) with him 15 days.
But of the other apostles (sent ones) I saw none, except James the Lord's brother.
Now the things which I write to you, look, before God, I do not lie.
Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia,
And was unknown by face to the churches of Judaea which were in Christ.
But they had heard only, that the man who persecuted (attacked for faith) us in times past now preaches the faith which he once destroyed.
And they glorified (praised) God in me.

verses.text: Then 14 years after, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.

And I went up by revelation (showing), and communicated (explained) to them that gospel (good news) which I preach among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), but privately to those who were of reputation (well-known leaders), lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain (for nothing).
But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled (forced) to be circumcised,

And that because of false brothers unawares brought in (sneaked in), who came in privily (secretly) to spy out our liberty (freedom) which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage (slavery).
To them we gave place (gave in) by subjection (obeying them), no, not for an hour, that the truth of the gospel (good news) might continue with you.

But of these who seemed to be somewhat (important), whatever they were, it makes no matter to me. God accepts no man's person (does not favor anyone). For those who seemed to be somewhat (important) in conference (talking with me) added nothing to me.

But on the other hand, they saw that the gospel (good news) of the uncircumcision (people who are not circumcised) was committed (trusted) to me, as the gospel (good news) of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews) was to Peter.

For He who worked effectually (powerfully) in Peter for the apostleship (being a sent one) of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews), the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).

And when James, Peter, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived (saw) the grace that was given to me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship (sharing), that we should go to the heathen (people who are not Jews), and they to the circumcision (the circumcised Jews).
Only they wanted that we should remember the poor, the same which I also was forward (eager) to do.
But when Peter had come to Antioch, I withstood (stood against) him to the face, because he was to be blamed.

For before certain men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). But when they had come, Peter withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews).
And the other Jews dissembled (pretended) likewise with him, so much that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation (pretending).

But when I saw that they did not walk uprightly according to the truth of the gospel (good news), I said to Peter before them all: If you, being a Jew, live after the manner of Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and not as do the Jews, why do you compel (force) the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) to live as do the Jews?
We who are Jews by nature (birth), and not sinners of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews),

Knowing that a person is not justified (made right with God) by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified (made right with God) by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law. For by the works of the law no flesh (person) will be justified (made right with God).
But if, while we seek to be justified (made right with God) by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is Christ therefore the minister (servant) of sin? God forbid.
For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor (lawbreaker).
For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live to God.

I am crucified with Christ. Nevertheless I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh (body) I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave Himself for me.
I do not frustrate (throw away) the grace of God. For if righteousness (being right with God) comes by the law, then Christ is dead in vain (died for nothing).

verses.text: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched (put a spell on) you, that you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ has been evidently (clearly) set forth, crucified among you?
This only would I learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now made perfect (complete) by the flesh (sinful self)?
Have you suffered so many things in vain (for nothing)? If it is yet in vain (for nothing).
He therefore who ministers (gives) to you the Spirit, and works miracles among you, does He do it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted (counted) to him for righteousness (being right with God).
Know therefore that those who are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

And the scripture, foreseeing (seeing ahead of time) that God would justify (make right with God) the heathen (people who are not Jews) through faith, preached before the gospel (good news) to Abraham, saying: In you will all nations be blessed.
So then those who are of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.
For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.
But that no one is justified (made right with God) by the law in the sight of God, it is evident (clear). For: The just (those who are right with God) will live by faith.
And the law is not of faith. But: The man who does them will live in them.
Christ has redeemed (bought back and set free) us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.
That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Brothers, I speak after the manner of men (in an everyday way). Though it is only a man's covenant (agreement), yet if it is confirmed, no one disannuls (cancels) it, or adds to it.
Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. God does not say: And to seeds, as of many. But as of one: And to your seed, which is Christ.

And this I say: The covenant (agreement) that was confirmed before by God in Christ, the law, which came 430 years after, cannot disannul (cancel), that it should make the promise of no effect (worthless).
For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise.

Why then does the law serve? It was added because of transgressions (lawbreaking), till the Seed should come to whom the promise was made. And it was ordained (set in order) by angels in the hand of a mediator (go-between).
Now a mediator (go-between) is not a mediator (go-between) of one, but God is one.
Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid. For if there had been a law given which could have given life, truly righteousness (being right with God) would have been by the law.
But the scripture has concluded (shut up) all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up to the faith which should afterwards be revealed (shown).
So the law was our schoolmaster (guardian) to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified (made right with God) by faith.
But after that faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster (guardian).
For you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.
For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond (slave) nor free, there is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

verses.text: Now I say, that the heir, as long as he is a child, differs nothing from a servant, though he is lord (owner) of all,
But is under tutors (guardians) and governors (managers) until the time appointed (set) by the father.
Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage (slavery) under the elements (basic rules) of the world.
But when the fulness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
To redeem (buy back and set free) those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption (being made God's children) of sons.
And because you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying: Abba (Daddy), Father.
So you are no more a servant, but a son. And if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
But then, when you did not know God, you did service (were slaves) to those which by nature are no gods.
But now, after you have known God, or rather are known by God, how do you turn again to the weak and beggarly (poor) elements (basic rules), to which you desire again to be in bondage (slavery)?
You observe (keep) days, and months, and times, and years.
I am afraid for you, lest I have bestowed (spent) labour (hard work) on you in vain (for nothing).
Brothers, I beseech (beg) you, be as I am, for I am as you are. You have not injured me at all.
You know how through infirmity (weakness) of the flesh (body) I preached the gospel (good news) to you at the first.
And my temptation (trial) which was in my flesh (body) you did not despise (look down on), nor reject. But you received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
Where is then the blessedness (happiness) you spoke of? For I bear you record (tell you truly), that, if it had been possible, you would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me.
Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
They zealously affect (eagerly seek after) you, but not well. Yes, they would exclude (shut out) you, that you might affect (eagerly seek after) them.
But it is good to be zealously affected (eagerly sought after) always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.
My little children, for whom I travail (have birth pains) in birth again until Christ is formed in you,
I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice (speak to you in a different way). For I stand in doubt of (am unsure about) you.
Tell me, you who desire to be under the law, do you not hear the law?
For it is written, that Abraham had 2 sons, the one by a bondmaid (slave woman), the other by a freewoman.
But he who was of the bondwoman (slave woman) was born after the flesh (in the natural way). But he of the freewoman was by promise.
Which things are an allegory (a story with a deeper meaning). For these are the 2 covenants (agreements): the one from the mount Sinai, which gives birth to bondage (slavery), which is Agar (Hagar).
For this Agar (Hagar) is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to (stands for) Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage (slavery) with her children.
But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.

For it is written: Rejoice, you barren (woman who cannot have children) who does not bear. Break forth and cry, you who do not travail (have birth pains). For the desolate (lonely woman) has many more children than she who has a husband.
Now we, brothers, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.
But as then he who was born after the flesh (in the natural way) persecuted (attacked) him who was born after the Spirit, even so it is now.
Nevertheless what does the scripture say? Cast out the bondwoman (slave woman) and her son. For the son of the bondwoman (slave woman) will not be heir with the son of the freewoman.
So then, brothers, we are not children of the bondwoman (slave woman), but of the free.

verses.text: Stand fast therefore in the liberty (freedom) with which Christ has made us free, and do not be entangled again with the yoke (wooden bar for working together) of bondage (slavery).
Look, I Paul say to you, that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit (help) you nothing.
For I testify again to every man who is circumcised, that he is a debtor (bound) to do the whole law.
Christ has become of no effect (no help) to you, whoever of you are justified (made right with God) by the law. You have fallen from grace.
For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness (being right with God) by faith.
For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision avails (counts for) anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith which works by love.
You did run well. Who did hinder (stop) you that you should not obey the truth?
This persuasion (way of thinking) does not come from Him who calls you.
A little leaven (yeast) leavens the whole lump (makes the whole batch of dough rise).
I have confidence in you through the Lord, that you will be no otherwise minded (think no other way). But whoever troubles you will bear their judgment, whoever they are.
And I, brothers, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution (being attacked for faith)? Then the offence (stumbling block) of the cross has ceased (stopped).
I wish that those who trouble you were even cut off.
For, brothers, you have been called to liberty (freedom). Only do not use liberty (freedom) for an occasion (excuse) to the flesh (sinful self), but by love serve one another.
For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: You will love your neighbour as yourself.
But if you bite and devour (eat up) one another, take heed (be careful) that you are not consumed (destroyed) one by another.
This I say then: Walk in the Spirit, and you will not fulfil the lust (wrong desire) of the flesh (sinful self).

For the flesh (sinful self) lusts (has wrong desires) against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh (sinful self). And these are contrary the one to the other, so that you cannot do the things that you would.
But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

Now the works of the flesh (sinful self) are manifest (plain to see), which are these: Adultery (being unfaithful in marriage), fornication (sexual sin), uncleanness (impure living), lasciviousness (shameless sexual desire),

Idolatry (worshipping idols), witchcraft, hatred, variance (fighting), emulations (jealous rivalry), wrath (anger), strife (quarrels), seditions (splitting into sides), heresies (false teaching groups),

Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings (wild parties), and such like. Of these I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering (patience), gentleness, goodness, faith,
Meekness (being gentle), temperance (self-control). Against such there is no law.
And those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh (sinful self) with the affections (passions) and lusts (wrong desires).
If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
Let us not be desirous of vain glory (empty pride), provoking one another, envying one another.

verses.text: Brothers, if anyone is overtaken (caught) in a fault, you who are spiritual, restore such a one in the spirit of meekness (gentleness), considering yourself, lest you also be tempted.
Bear (carry) one another's burdens (heavy loads), and so fulfil the law of Christ.
For if anyone thinks themselves to be something, when they are nothing, they deceive (fool) themselves.
But let everyone prove (test) their own work, and then they will have rejoicing in themselves alone, and not in another.
For everyone will bear (carry) their own burden (load).
Let the one who is taught in the word communicate (share) to the one who teaches in all good things.
Do not be deceived (fooled). God is not mocked (made fun of). For whatever a person sows (plants), that they will also reap (harvest).

For whoever sows (plants) to their flesh (sinful self) will of the flesh (sinful self) reap (harvest) corruption (decay). But whoever sows (plants) to the Spirit will of the Spirit reap (harvest) life everlasting.
And let us not be weary in well doing (doing good). For in due season (at the right time) we will reap (harvest), if we do not faint (lose heart).
As we therefore have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who are of the household (family) of faith.
You see how large a letter I have written to you with my own hand.

As many as desire to make a fair show (look good) in the flesh (on the outside), they constrain (force) you to be circumcised, only lest they should suffer persecution (being attacked for faith) for the cross of Christ.
For neither do they themselves who are circumcised keep the law, but desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory (brag) in your flesh (body).
But God forbid that I should glory (brag), except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails (counts for) anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature (creation).
And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and on the Israel of God.
From now on let no one trouble me, for I bear (carry) in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.
Brothers, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
